Whether a closed row revoked differs from its closure by the channel's name

log_closure_named_by_channel.Rd

RF1 and RF4 of the review of the correction of F1 of the 0.29.0, way (b) restricted, decided on 2026-11-25, beside the way (a) of the identity door. A closed row is sealed by its closure under the empty name. A round that writes the name on it and does not seal the row (on the row set back to active, a round stopped or held; under the 0.28.0, a round that did not act), followed by the owner putting the row back to revoked, leaves the row differing from the closure by that name alone, written by the channel: the round would hold it with no author, and ask its owner to approve the channel's own write while the revocation waits.

Usage

log_closure_named_by_channel(events, record, row, seal, channel_account = NULL)

Arguments

events

The row's log, as register_log() returns it.

record

The record id to look at.

row

The row as read, a data frame of one row.

seal

The seal the round believes for the row.

channel_account

The REDCap usernames that hold the round's token, one or more, or NULL when they are not configured.

Value

TRUE or FALSE.

Details

TRUE only when all of these hold, and the caller asks it only of a closed row whose change has no author, log_pending_authors():

  • the channel's account is configured and the row asks for revoked;

  • the row as read, with its name emptied, gives the seal the round believes, the closure's: every other intent field is the closure's;

  • in the row's log, above the newest execution, every write of username is the channel's, and the newest one wrote the name the row holds.

It only lets a revocation go on: a row that asks for an access, or with any other difference from the closure, or a name written by anybody else, is judged as before.
